steps.text: Checking whether a PowerShell process was spawned from services.exe for this modify-existing-service test, I consider searching the registry ImagePath key, but the Fax service path search already returned nothing, so I'll skip further lookups and submit.
I'm calling this malicious. It's an Atomic Red Team style test of T1543.003 (modifying an existing service), not routine administration.

submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user WORKSTATION5\wardog ran an interactive cmd.exe (proc-690e6c933a) at High integrity. From it: (1) 00:45:33, sc.exe (proc-f4d3576242) changed the Fax service binPath to 'powershell.exe -noexit -c "write-host 'T1543.003 Test'"'; (2) 00:45:35, 'sc start Fax' (proc-cd222a569d) started the service so the PowerShell payload would run as SYSTEM; (3) 00:45:41, sc.exe (proc-babd722e6c) set binPath back to fxssvc.exe to cover the change. This matches Atomic Red Team T1543.003 (Modify Existing Service): hijacking a service for persistence or privilege escalation. The test marker means this is probably an emulation, but the technique is malicious, so the response treats it as real. Cleanup: confirm the Fax ImagePath is back to fxssvc.exe, and rotate the wardog credentials.
